readingInstruction: Read Luke 4:14-5:39. Jesus preaches in Nazareth, is rejected, begins to heal and call disciples, and meets his first controversies. Read 4:18-21 slowly. It is the mission statement of the whole Gospel.
settingTheScene: Jesus returns to Galilee in the power of the Spirit. He goes to the synagogue in Nazareth, his hometown, as was his custom, and he is handed the scroll of Isaiah. The reading he chooses is from Isaiah 61, which describes the anointed one who will bring good news to the poor. What he says next, and how the people respond, sets the pattern for his ministry: great grace and great opposition.
observation: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor” (4:18).
“He has sent me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty those who are oppressed” (4:18).
“Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing” (4:21).
“Truly, I say to you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown” (4:24).
“But he would withdraw to desolate places and pray” (5:16).
“Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord” (5:8).
“Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching men” (5:10).
“I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance” (5:32).
interpretation:
In Nazareth, Jesus reads the words of Isaiah and sits down, as a teacher does. Every eye is fastened on him. “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” That is a stunning claim. He is the anointed one of Isaiah 61: the Spirit is upon him, and he brings good news to the poor, freedom to captives, sight to the blind, and release to the oppressed. The “year of the Lord’s favor” is the jubilee, the great year of release.

The people at first marvel at his gracious words. But then he reminds them that God sent Elijah to a widow in Sidon and Elisha to heal Naaman the Syrian, both Gentiles, while Israel’s own needy were passed over. The hometown crowd erupts in fury and tries to throw him off a cliff. The pattern is set. The good news will go to outsiders, and many insiders will reject it. Jesus passes through the midst of them and goes away.

In Capernaum, he teaches with authority, casts out a demon, heals Peter’s mother-in-law, and heals many at sundown. Luke notes that he withdraws to pray in desolate places. Even when crowds clamor for him, he keeps to his mission: “I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns also; for I was sent for this purpose.”

The miraculous catch of fish leads to Peter’s confession. Seeing the power of Jesus, Peter does not rejoice but falls at his knees, saying, “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man.” The presence of holiness exposes sin. Jesus does not depart. He says, “Do not be afraid,” and calls Peter to follow. Peter, James, and John leave everything.

Then come the first controversies: Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man, calls Levi the tax collector, and eats with sinners. The Pharisees grumble, and Jesus answers: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.” He then speaks of new wine in new wineskins. The new covenant cannot be poured into the old forms.
connection: Isaiah 61:1-2 and 58:6 stand behind Jesus’ reading. Leviticus 25 describes the year of jubilee. 1 Kings 17:8-16 and 2 Kings 5 are the Old Testament stories Jesus cites. Isaiah 6:5 shows the prophet’s cry, “Woe is me!” before the holy God. Mark 2:17 has the parallel on the physician. 2 Corinthians 5:17 says that if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. John 1:11 says he came to his own, and his own people did not receive him.
application:
Read Isaiah 61:1-2 slowly and ask where Jesus has done this in your life.

Notice Jesus’ habit of slipping away to pray. Plan a regular time and place for it.

Like Peter, bring your sinfulness to Jesus without hiding it, and hear him say, “Do not be afraid.”
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for bringing good news to the poor, liberty to captives, and sight to the blind.
Tell him what you need him to set free in you.
Ask him to teach you to follow.
